'PyDictUnicodeEntry.me_hash' (`entry_ptr->me_hash`) is accessed under a critical section at insert_to_emptydict:2118 but is read plainly here, with nothing synchronising it. A lock held by only some accessors of a field serialises nothing: the guarded and unguarded accessors race each other. This is the shape of gh-153298 (ga_parameters / CPY-0025), gh-128714 (func.__annotations__ / CPY-0029) and gh-153908 (itertools count_repr). Py_ssize_t does not tear on LP64, so the visible effect is a stale value rather than memory unsafety — one FT_ATOMIC_* on each access is the fix. Guarded twin: insert_to_emptydict:2118.

'result' becomes reachable from other threads at _PyObject_GC_TRACK() (line 1762), and 'fill' is still written afterwards, in set_add_entry():342, with a plain non-atomic store and no critical section. On a free-threaded build another thread can observe the object between the two — half-initialised, and torn if the store is wider than a word. Finish initialising before publishing, or make the tail stores atomic. This is the fixup_slot_dispatchers shape (gh-151377).
